problem: Existing embodied-AI simulators have little scene diversity: most model only homes, and even Behavior-1K covers just 8 scene types. Their tasks are narrow, they rarely combine physically realistic learned low-level control for legged robots, and they have no language-capable social NPCs. Policies trained there struggle to generalize to service-oriented, real-world settings.
motivation: Collecting real robot data at scale is expensive and hard to transfer across hardware, so the authors argue that Sim2Real on diverse, interactive, annotated scenes is key to scaling embodied learning. General robots are likely to be deployed first in service venues such as supermarkets and hospitals. Serving humans often requires resolving ambiguous instructions through dialogue. Most prior benchmarks also teleport or animate the agent rather than drive it with a physical controller, which hides a large sim-to-real gap.
key_idea: Build a city-scale, fully interactive Isaac Sim society made of three parts: GRScenes (100k designer scenes across 89 categories with hierarchical annotations), GRResidents (LLM-driven NPCs that query a scene-graph World Knowledge Manager to generate tasks and answer questions), and GRBench (object nav, social nav and loco-manipulation tasks executed by legged robots through RL-trained control APIs).
insight: Physically realistic low-level control makes tasks much harder than they look under oracle/teleport actions. With collision-free shortest paths, point-to-point locomotion SR drops from 100% on flat ground to 58% (H1) and 14% (Aliengo+Z1) in a furnished house, and manipulation SR drops from 100% to 8%; the authors attribute this mainly to path/motion-planning failures. Loco-manipulation ends at 0 SR for every backbone. Across baselines, a modular LLM agent (SegFormer perception + BEV occupancy map + candidate selection by an LLM + RRT* + RL controller) beats end-to-end VLM action selection on Object Loco-Nav: 22.00 test SR with ChatGLM3 vs 14.00 for the GPT-4o VLM. Allowing more NPC dialogue rounds raises Social Loco-Nav SR from 6.00 (0 rounds) to 24.00 (4 rounds), although the trend is non-monotonic (8.00 at 2 rounds). The perception diagnostic is internally inconsistent: the text says Qwen-VL perception is better, but the table shows GPT-4o slightly higher on object-nav SR (8.00 vs 6.00).
method: GRScenes: about 100k designer-made synthetic scenes in 89 functional categories (~30% non-home) that can be composed into city blocks. The initial release is 100 curated scenes (70 home, 30 commercial) with 2,956 interactive and 22,001 non-interactive objects from 96 categories; interactive objects carry part labels (X-form in Omniverse), material labels, BEV polygon region labels, and object captions drafted by GPT-4V from multi-view renders and then human-checked.

World Knowledge Manager (WKM): maintains a per-step scene graph (object nodes; Sr3D spatial relations plus in/out-of edges) built from annotations and simulator state. It exposes find_diff (coarse-to-fine priority: category > room > relation > appearance), get_info and filter APIs, plus a grounding API.

GRResidents LLM NPC: a memory of chat history, an LLM programmer that iteratively calls WKM APIs to retrieve scene knowledge, and an LLM speaker that generates responses. The NPC is used for task and instruction generation and as an oracle answering agent questions. Tested with GPT-4o, InternLM2-Chat-20B and Llama-3-70B.

Robot control APIs: RL locomotion policies trained in Isaac Gym for Unitree H1, G1, Fourier GR-1 and Aliengo+Z1, plus manipulation via IK. Physics runs at 1/240 s, the controller at 60 Hz and high-level planning/rendering at 1 Hz. A reset function re-stands a fallen robot and is counted as the RT metric.

GRBench: Object Loco-Navigation (unique language description of a target), Social Loco-Navigation (coarse instruction, at most 3 Ask rounds with the NPC) and Loco-Manipulation (pick-and-place under at most 2 spatial conditions). Each has 300 episodes (100 val / 200 test) with 7–20 m collision-free GT paths sampled on a 1.4 cm occupancy grid. Nav success means the target is in the FoV within 3 m, with STOP required within 14,400 physics steps. New metrics are ECR (excluded candidate rate) and SCR (satisfied condition rate).

Zero-shot VLM baseline: the current RGB frame plus a prompt go to a VLM (GPT-4o, Qwen-VL or InternVL-Chat-1.5), which picks 1 of 12 macro-actions (forward / diagonal-left / diagonal-right 2/4/6 m, turn 90°, stop), plus Ask/Pick/Place where the task allows.

LLM agent baseline: the grounding module runs SegFormer on RGB-D with robot state to produce candidate point clouds and 2D/3D boxes. A memory module keeps a BEV occupancy map with candidate descriptions and dialogue info. An LLM decision module selects the candidate goal or writes a question to the NPC. The action module plans with RRT* (replanning on map updates) executed by the RL locomotion policy, and uses IK plus distance-threshold attach for grasping.

setting.backbone: Frozen LLMs as decision modules (GPT-4o, Qwen, Llama-3 8B, InternLM-2-Chat, ChatGLM3) with SegFormer perception and RRT*; zero-shot VLM baselines (GPT-4o, Qwen-VL, InternVL-Chat-1.5); low-level RL locomotion policies (trained in Isaac Gym) for Unitree H1 / Aliengo+Z1
setting.model_size: mixed (e.g., Llama-3 8B in the agent; GPT-4o size undisclosed; NPCs use InternLM2-Chat-20B / Llama-3-70B / GPT-4o)
setting.training_data: none (training-free) for the high-level agents. RL locomotion policies are trained in Isaac Gym, with details withheld. The platform itself provides about 100k scenes, of which 100 annotated scenes are released initially.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (H1 head camera; for Aliengo, a camera on a pole 0.8 m above the base) + robot state; the VLM baseline uses only the current RGB frame + text prompt
setting.action_space: VLM baseline: 12 discrete macro-actions (move forward / advance diagonally left/right 2/4/6 m, turn left/right 90°, stop) + Ask (social) + Pick/Place (manipulation). LLM agent: choose a candidate goal object, then an RRT* path executed as continuous legged locomotion by the RL controller; IK arm control for pick/place.
setting.privileged: The agent receives the robot state/pose. The Social task uses an oracle LLM NPC with full scene-graph knowledge. A fallen robot is reset to standing (counted as RT). Grasping is simplified: the object attaches to the gripper within a distance threshold. No GT map or semantics is given to the agent (SegFormer perception, online occupancy map).

numbers_note: TL here is the paper's PL (path length). ECR values are on inconsistent scales in Table 4 (e.g., 17.79 vs 1.02). Loco-Manipulation PL values are around 0.1–0.3 and are unexplained. All backbones score SR 0 on Loco-Manipulation. Only a subset of the Table 4 backbones is listed; the others are Qwen-VL, InternVL-Chat-1.5 and the LLMs Llama-3 8B and InternLM-2-Chat, with Random at SR 2.50 val obj-nav. Omitted secondary results: (1) Table 5 diagnostic on 50 val episodes, swapping the perception VLM. Obj-nav SR is 8.00 with GPT-4o vs 6.00 with Qwen-VL; social SR is 12.00 for both. This contradicts the text's claim that Qwen-VL is superior. (2) Table 6 on allowed dialogue rounds 0–4 (SR 6.00/10.00/8.00/17.00/24.00; split unspecified). Round 0 shows SPL 14.58 > SR 6.00, which is inconsistent. (3) The oracle-action (teleport) vs RL-controller comparison is described only qualitatively, with no numbers. (4) NPC referring/grounding/QA (Table 2) and controller evaluations (Table 3) are platform results, not nav benchmarks. The action list in the text says forward 2/4/6 m, but the prompt says 2/4/5 m.
results: On the 200-episode test split of Object Loco-Navigation, the best LLM-agent baselines reach 22.00 SR (ChatGLM3) and 21.50 SR (InternLM-2-Chat, SPL 12.45). The best zero-shot VLM (GPT-4o) reaches 14.00 SR, and random reaches only 2.50 SR on val. Social Loco-Navigation is harder: the best is Qwen at 14.00 val / 12.50 test SR, versus 7.00 for GPT-4o. Loco-Manipulation gives 0 SR for every backbone, due to frequent resets of the wide Aliengo base and arm collisions. The resulting difficulty gradation shows that realistic legged control plus high-level planning is far from solved.
limitations: Only 100 of the ~100k scenes (7 building types) and one city block were released initially because of licensing. Locomotion-policy training details are withheld, and the real-world H1 demo is qualitative only and was not yet released.

The benchmark is small (100 val / 200 test episodes per task), results vary strongly across LLM backbones, and there are internal inconsistencies (diagnostic text vs table, SPL > SR in the dialogue ablation, inconsistent ECR scales).

The NPCs have oracle scene-graph knowledge and no physical contact. Loco-manipulation relies on simplified attach-grasping yet still yields 0 SR, so it offers no discriminative signal among current methods.
